question: India's first high-speed rail line is being constructed between (as of February 2022):
solution:
The correct answer is** ****__Mumbai-Ahmedabad__**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first high-speed railway corridor under construction is currently under construction between **Mumbai and Ahmedabad** (508 km (316 mi)) with a designed maximum operational speed of 320 km/h (199 mph).
 
• **Surat** will be the first station to be constructed between Mumbai- Ahmedabad route, set for the country's first bullet train, informed an official privy to the developments on Wednesday. “The work on the four stations (Vapi, Bilimora, Surat, Bharuch) has expedited and they will be ready by December 2024.​ 
 
• The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project states that just 21 km of the total 508.17 km of rail track will be buried and the remainder will be elevated.
 
• The mangroves and bird refuge along Thane Creek will be safeguarded by the tunnel.
 
• To maintain this station illuminated by natural light, a dedicated skylight provision has also been built, according to a railway official involved in the project's execution.
 
• As part of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor, tunnel construction for the twin line between Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) and Shilphata in Maharashtra has begun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Mumbai Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor will only have one subterranean station, and that station is the BKC station, on which construction began on Thursday.
 
• The first railway on Indian sub-continent ran over a stretch of 21 miles from **Bombay to Thane**. The idea of a railway to connect **Bombay with Thane,** **Kalyan and with the Thal** and **Bhore Ghats** inclines first occurred to Mr. George Clark, the Chief Engineer of the Bombay Government, during a visit to Bhandup in 1843.
 
• **Mumbai-Pune:**
 
 
• ​India's **first 6-lane wide concrete**, access-controlled toll motorway is the** Mumbai-Pune Expressway, or Yashwantrao Chavan Expressway.**
 
• It connects Pune, the cultural and educational centre of Maharashtra, with Mumbai, the state capital of Maharashtra and the financial centre of India, across a distance of** 94.5 kilometers.**
 
• The motorway, which went into **full operation in 2002**, raised the speed and safety standards for driving on Indian highways.
 
• It is one of the** busiest roads **in India.​
 
 
 
• **Delhi-Meerut:**
 
 
• **​**The **82.15 km (51.05 mi) long**, semi-high speed rail corridor known as the Delhi-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System (Delhi-Meerut RRTS) would **link Meerut, Delhi, and Ghaziabad.**
 
• It is one of three rapid rail routes planned as part of Phase I of the Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) project, which is overseen by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC).
 
• The travel time from Delhi to Meerut will be less than an hour at a **top speed of 180 km/h (111.85 mph)**.
 
• The project will include **24 stations**, including two depots at Duhai and Modipuram, and will cost 30,274 crore (US$3.8 billion).
 
 
 
• **Delhi-****Mumbai:**
 
 
• **​**The **1,350 km long, 8 lanes wide** (expandable to 12 lanes), access-controlled Delhi-Mumbai Expressway connects Mumbai with New Delhi, the nation's capital of India, and is currently under development. 
 
• On **March 8, 2019**, Nitin Gadkari, a union minister, formally set the project's cornerstone in the presence of Sushma Swaraj and Arun Jaitley. 
 
• A rough estimate of the project's entire value, including the cost of acquiring the land, is** 1,00,000 crores ($13.1 billion).** 
 
• The NHAI would also build a further 31 km-long spur on this highway from** Noida International Airport in Jewar to Sector-65**, Faridabad (DND–KMP Expressway).
